meta.storyTitle: Each round's findings are rendered and presented through a new review-report docgen document

q62f7c578.question: The contract section's renderReviewReport signature currently lists three parameters (call, findings, reconciliation); error-paths/test-strategy identified that a fourth parameter, priorFindings: readonly Finding[] | undefined, is required so each ReconciliationResult.priorFindingRef can be resolved back to the prior finding's own category/severity for a meaningful inline annotation. The Task implementing this Story must carry the corrected four-parameter signature.
q62f7c578.choice: Add priorFindings as a fourth parameter
q62f7c578.rationale: ReconciliationResult only carries priorFindingRef + verdict (sc3's own interfaceSketch), not the prior finding's own category/severity -- renderReviewReport needs priorFindings: readonly Finding[] | undefined (the exact set s3's reconcileRound was called with) to render a meaningful annotation. The implementing Task carries this corrected four-parameter signature: (call, findings, reconciliation, priorFindings).

q8c471cdf.question: The contract section's api.errors lists type 'Error' for an invalid round; error-paths names this specifically as a RangeError (mirroring runReviewRound's own RangeError for an invalid round). The Task implementing this Story must align to RangeError.
q8c471cdf.rationale: Matches error-paths' own detail and the established runReviewRound precedent (src/workflow/review-round/driver.ts), which already throws a RangeError for an invalid round -- removes ambiguity rather than leaving a broad Error type that undersells the actual, more specific contract.

49e11a57.question: The contract section's api[0].returns is documented as Promise<string>, but insrc_present (confirmed directly against its real handler, src/mcp/server.ts's handleInsrcPresent) can never present a plain file like a review-report: its matching is scoped entirely to the daemon's pending-workflow-artifact list, and a review-report is never pending approval (k3; ac3 itself says 'no response required from the user'). This fails ac3's presentation requirement and should have been caught during design -- ac3 named the wrong mechanism.
49e11a57.choice: Return { path, markdown } instead of a bare path
49e11a57.rationale: insrc_present's matching is scoped entirely to the daemon's pending-workflow-artifact list (confirmed directly against the real handler); a review-report structurally can never appear there. Returning the rendered markdown alongside the path lets the caller present it directly in its own response -- the same convention this codebase's own agents already use for review packets and self-reviews -- with no tool call needed at all, which is the only way to actually satisfy ac3. The testStrategy subject/ac3 proving-test name is corrected the same way, from the old "...so insrc_present can open it..." wording to one that states what the test actually proves.

summary.prose: Story s4 adds renderReviewReport (sc4): a function the round-driver calls once per round, after that round's own findings (and, for round>1, s3's reconciliation classification) are in hand, to render the round's outcome into a persisted Markdown artifact under the review's own .insrc/tmp/<reviewId>/ directory. For a correction round it annotates each prior HIGH/MED finding with the verdict s3's reconciliation pass already computed (confirmed/still-open/contradicted/no-longer-surfaced), scoped to only that one adjacent round pair -- never a running audit of the full review history. The round-driver then presents the written path to the user via insrc_present every round.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: Alternative a2 wins: one shared round-driver function in a new sibling module under src/workflow/ (outside review-history/, which is being retired from rather than extended) takes a small per-review-type hook set -- the grounding/findings call, checkpoint granularity, and finding taxonomy/severity -- and runs the identical round cycle, checkpoint lifecycle, and reconciliation call for every review type.

ownedContracts.name: Review-report docgen call shape
ownedContracts.purpose: The explicit, agent-invoked call shape that renders a round's findings (+ relevant reconciliation annotations) to a persisted MD artifact, per k6.

consumedContracts.name: Review-type hook set
consumedContracts.purpose: The small hook set (grounding/findings call, checkpoint granularity, taxonomy/severity) that is the only thing legitimately differing per review type, consumed by the round-driver, per the Epic's one-shared-process framing (Story s1 ac1/ac2).

consumedContracts.name: Finding taxonomy + severity scale
consumedContracts.purpose: The fixed design-review-specific taxonomy and the per-review-type-configurable severity scale every finding carries, per lc1/lc2.

boundary.internal: The exact docgen docType registration and MD rendering logic (including the resolved/still-open/contradicted annotation rule scoped to this round's own corrections) stay internal to s4; no other Story's type depends on the renderer's internals.

adjacentBoundaries.internal: The round-driver function itself -- what it does internally to run the grounding+findings, reconciliation, render+present and checkpoint-write cycle -- stays private to s1; no other Story's type depends on the driver's internals, only on the hook contract sc1 exposes.

Which exact per-review-type severity scales exist beyond the HIGH/MED default, and how a review type's Feedback implementation declares its own, stay internal to s2; no other Story's type depends on Finding's shape.

How the reconciliation LLM call is actually prompted, and how it reads the temp folder's audit trail when needed, stay internal to s3; no other Story's type depends on ReconciliationResult's internals beyond its verdict shape.

The exact per-review-type granularity mapping (round-level for design review, per-Task for code review) and the durable-copy-before-deletion mechanics stay internal to s5; no other Story's type depends on ReviewCheckpoint's internals beyond what sc1's round-driver needs to call it.

hldContextSlice.rolloutPhase: Phase B — taxonomy, reconciliation, rendering, checkpointing

nonFunctional.performance: Checkpoint write/read (sc5) is a single small JSON file write/read per completed unit of work (a round, or a Task), adding no I/O beyond what the round cycle already performs.
nonFunctional.durability: The final round's review-output JSON is copied into durable artifact storage before the .insrc/tmp/<reviewId>/ folder is deleted at a terminal state (k7), so a completed review's result survives after the ephemeral working folder is gone.

api.name: renderReviewReport
api.signature: function renderReviewReport(call: ReviewReportDocgenCall, findings: readonly Finding[], reconciliation: readonly ReconciliationResult[] | undefined, priorFindings: readonly Finding[] | undefined): Promise<{ readonly path: string; readonly markdown: string }>

parameters.name: call
parameters.purpose: Identifies which round of which review this call renders -- exactly sc4's interfaceSketch, the HLD's own named call shape.

parameters.name: findings
parameters.purpose: This round's own finalized, self-contained finding set (produced by s1's round-driver per k4) -- rendered as this round's own report section; never re-derived or re-grounded by this call.

parameters.name: reconciliation
parameters.purpose: For round>1, s3's reconcileRound output classifying the prior round's HIGH/MED findings against this round's findings -- rendered as inline resolved/still-open/contradicted/no-longer-surfaced annotations (ac2/lc3). Undefined for round 1, where no prior round exists to reconcile against.

returns.type: Promise<{ readonly path: string; readonly markdown: string }>
returns.meaning: The persisted file's path AND the exact markdown written to it. The caller presents `markdown` directly in its own response to satisfy ac3 -- insrc_present never applies to a review-report (see resolved question 49e11a57).

errors.condition: call.reviewId fails the same literal-identifier validation s3's reconcileRound already enforces (requireValidReviewId) -- rejected before any path is joined or any file is written.
call.round is not a positive integer.

preconditions: findings is this round's own finalized, self-contained finding set -- never re-derived or re-grounded by this call
reconciliation, when provided, is s3's reconcileRound output for the (round-1, round) adjacent pair only, never a multi-round accumulation
postconditions: Exactly one Markdown file is written under the reviewed repository's .insrc/tmp/<call.reviewId>/ directory for this round, matching k7's own listing of what the temp folder holds before terminal-state deletion
The returned path points to that exact file

dataModelChanges.details: interface ReviewReportDocgenCall { readonly reviewId: string; readonly round: number; } -- exactly sc4's HLD interfaceSketch, used as renderReviewReport's own identifying first parameter.

interactionWithShared.howDetails: ReviewReportDocgenCall and renderReviewReport are authored here as sc4's concrete shape, implementing the HLD interfaceSketch verbatim as renderReviewReport's first parameter and adding the findings/reconciliation parameters the render logic itself needs -- the same precedent sc3/reconcileRound already established, whose own bare interfaceSketch likewise omitted reconcileRound's full parameter list.

This Story's contract does not reference RoundDriverHooks fields directly -- renderReviewReport is called by s1's round-driver cycle once reviewKind/checkpointGranularity have already shaped that cycle; s4 only needs the findings and reconciliation results the cycle already produced at that point.
findings: readonly Finding[] is read directly -- each finding's id/category/severity is rendered verbatim; this Story does not redefine Finding's shape.

reconciliation: readonly ReconciliationResult[] | undefined is read directly -- each result's verdict becomes that prior finding's inline annotation, keyed by priorFindingRef back to the finding it refers to; this Story does not redefine ReconciliationResult's shape or recompute verdicts. The HLD's own sc3.consumedByStories and s4's boundary.depends do not yet list this dependency even though ac1/ac2 require it -- see the hld.amendmentProposal submitted at the contract.detail step, which declares it explicitly.

errorCases.scenario: call.reviewId contains a path-traversal or otherwise non-literal segment (e.g. '../../../private')
errorCases.detection: A literal-identifier regex check (matching s3's own requireValidReviewId, src/workflow/review-round/reconciliation.ts) run before any path is joined.
errorCases.response: Throws synchronously before any filesystem access, rather than joining the value into the write path unvalidated.
errorCases.userImpact: The round-driver's render call fails outright for this round rather than silently writing outside the review's own .insrc/tmp/<reviewId>/ directory.

errorCases.scenario: call.round is not a positive integer
errorCases.detection: Number.isInteger(call.round) && call.round >= 1 check, mirroring runReviewRound's own round validation (src/workflow/review-round/driver.ts).
errorCases.response: Throws a RangeError synchronously before any write.
errorCases.userImpact: The caller sees an immediate, specific failure rather than a file silently written under a round-0 or fractional-round filename.

errorCases.scenario: The reviewed repository cannot be resolved (no registered repo for the request's cwd, and no INSRC_REPO fallback) -- the exact class of defect s3's reconciliation.ts needed three external review rounds to fully fix
errorCases.detection: resolveRepoPath (the canonical precedence resolver, src/daemon/steps/resolve-repo.ts) returns undefined.
errorCases.response: Rejects rather than silently defaulting to the daemon process's own cwd, applying the identical fix s3's reconcileRound already required.
errorCases.userImpact: The round's render step fails outright rather than writing the Markdown file under the wrong repository's temp folder.

errorCases.scenario: The write to .insrc/tmp/<reviewId>/ fails (disk full, permission denied, directory cannot be created)
errorCases.detection: The underlying filesystem write call rejects.
errorCases.response: renderReviewReport propagates the rejection unchanged rather than returning a path to a file that was never actually written.
errorCases.userImpact: The round-driver sees the render step as having failed outright, rather than receiving a path to a nonexistent file it might hand to insrc_present.

edgeCases.expected: reconciliation and priorFindings are both undefined/omitted; the rendered MD shows only this round's own findings with no annotation section at all -- not an empty annotation section, since there is nothing to reconcile against.

edgeCases.input: findings is an empty array (this round found nothing)
edgeCases.expected: The rendered MD still renders successfully, showing an explicit 'no findings this round' statement rather than an empty or malformed section.

edgeCases.input: reconciliation is provided (round>1) but describing what each priorFindingRef actually refers to requires the prior round's own Finding objects, which ReconciliationResult does not carry (it only carries priorFindingRef + verdict, per sc3's own interfaceSketch)
edgeCases.expected: renderReviewReport's signature therefore also takes priorFindings: readonly Finding[] | undefined -- the exact prior-round finding set s3's reconcileRound was called with -- alongside reconciliation, so each ReconciliationResult.priorFindingRef can be resolved back to that prior finding's own category/severity for a meaningful inline annotation. This corrects the contract section's initial two-parameter signature (call, findings, reconciliation), which omitted this third parameter; the Task that implements this Story must carry the corrected four-parameter signature (call, findings, reconciliation, priorFindings).

edgeCases.input: reconciliation contains a priorFindingRef with no matching entry in the supplied priorFindings
edgeCases.expected: That annotation is rendered with its verdict alone, naming the bare priorFindingRef since no richer description is available -- renderReviewReport never throws for a lookup miss here, since s3's own reconciliation contract guarantees the id itself (not the lookup) is correct, and a rendering gap is not a reason to fail the whole round's report.

invariantsToPreserve.text: A round's review-report MD shows only that round's own findings, with inline annotations limited to whichever prior findings this round's own reconciliation pass actually classified -- never a running audit of all history (lc3).
findings is this round's own full, independently re-grounded set -- never re-derived or re-grounded by this call (k4).
Reconciliation is a separate, already-completed dedicated pass; this call never performs its own reconciliation or re-grounding (k5).

testStrategy.testFramework: node:test, run via npx tsx --test, with a compile-time @ts-expect-error fixture for ReviewReportDocgenCall checked through a throwaway tsconfig (matches this Epic's s1/s2/s3 convention)

testLevels.purpose: Prove renderReviewReport writes exactly one persisted Markdown file under the review's own temp directory and returns its path (ac1), that round-1 vs round>1 rendering differs exactly as lc3/ac2 require, and the error/edge behaviors error-paths names.

for round greater than 1, the rendered Markdown inlines each reconciliation result's verdict next to the prior finding it refers to (via priorFindings), limited to only the findings this round's own reconciliation classified -- never a running audit of all history

a non-positive-integer round is rejected with a RangeError before any write

alternativesConsidered.name: Standalone render-to-Markdown function, not wired into the existing HTML/SVG docgen registry
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: A dedicated reviewReportDocgen(reviewId, round) call composes the round's Finding[] (+ReconciliationResult[] for round>1) directly into a Markdown string and persists it, independent of src/docgen/'s diagram framework.
alternativesConsidered.approach: A single function (the Epic's own 'review-report docgen' call, sc4) takes reviewId and round, reads the round's own findings and -- for round>1 -- the reconciliation result (both already in hand from s1's round-driver cycle, never re-derived), and renders them to a Markdown string: a heading, the round's findings grouped/annotated by category+severity, and (round>1 only) inline resolved/still-open/contradicted annotations limited to the specific prior Feedback items the submitter's corrections entries addressed or rejected this round (ac2/lc3). It writes that Markdown to a persisted path and returns it, matching ac1's literal 'persisted MD artifact' wording. It is never registered into src/docgen/registry.ts's InMemoryDocTypeRegistry -- that registry's own contract (DocumentIR -> RenderedDocumentShell) is diagram-first (derived graph nodes/edges rendered to a self-contained HTML/SVG shell per the how-does-it-work grounding), a shape with no natural meaning for a findings list, and handleDocgen itself never persists to disk anyway.
pros: Matches ac1's literal, repeated wording ('persisted MD artifact') exactly -- no translation step from HTML to MD, no empty/meaningless derived.nodes/edges

Smallest shape that fully meets ac1-ac3: one function, one Markdown composer, one write -- no new registry entry, no DocumentIR/RenderedDocumentShell plumbing to satisfy for a capability (diagrams) this Story does not need

Stays inside the Story's own internal boundary ('the exact docgen docType registration and MD rendering logic... stay internal to s4') without forcing that internal logic through a shared, diagram-oriented framework's external contract
cons: Does not reuse src/docgen/'s registry at all, so a reader expecting 'docgen' to mean 'the insrc_docgen tool' specifically must learn this Story's own narrower usage of the term
If a future Story wants the review-report to also render as an HTML/diagram view, this alternative does not provide that path for free

alternativesConsidered.name: Register a literal 'review-report' docType into the existing src/docgen/ HTML/SVG registry
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Add a DocTypeRegistration (src/docgen/registry.ts) whose extract() returns a DocumentIR with empty derived.nodes/edges and the round's findings/reconciliation rendered as narrated.sections prose, producing a RenderedDocumentShell.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Follow the exact pattern narrativeRegistration (src/docgen/extract/narrative.ts) uses: register 'review-report' with its own extractorInputSchema ({reviewId, round}), an extract() that builds a DocumentIR (derived.nodes/edges left empty -- a findings list has no diagram shape -- narrated.sections carrying the findings/reconciliation as prose), rendered through the shared shell to a self-contained offline HTML file with diagramFormat:'svg' (literal) and an inlined SVG runtime it will never actually use.
pros: Reuses an existing, well-established registration pattern (InMemoryDocTypeRegistry + toSerializable) instead of inventing a new render/persist mechanism
Automatically surfaces on all three existing docgen access surfaces (daemon tool, IPC, MCP) without extra wiring, per that framework's own k4 guarantee
cons: Produces an HTML file (RenderedDocumentShell), not the Markdown artifact ac1 explicitly and repeatedly requires -- violates ac1's literal wording, not just its spirit

handleDocgen never persists its own output to disk (confirmed by direct reading of src/mcp/docgen/handler.ts:67-94) -- this Story would still need to write its own persistence step on top, so the registry buys nothing toward ac1's actual requirement
Forces an empty, meaningless derived.nodes/edges on every call, misusing a type (DocumentIR) whose whole point is a structural diagram/prose partition for a payload that has no diagram at all
diagramFormat:'svg' and supportsZoomPan:true are literal fields on RenderedDocumentShell -- shipping them for a document with no diagram is actively misleading to any future reader of that shell
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Violates ac1 and sc4 directly on their own literal wording (an HTML shell is not a persisted MD artifact), and still requires its own separate disk-write step on top since handleDocgen never persists -- the registration buys reuse of a dispatch mechanism while failing the actual acceptance requirement it exists to satisfy.

alternativesConsidered.name: Both: register a diagram-shaped docType AND a separate Markdown writer
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Do a2's registration for discoverability on the existing docgen surfaces, plus a1's standalone Markdown writer for the actual persisted artifact ac1 requires.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Register 'review-report' into src/docgen/registry.ts (as in a2) purely so it is enumerable alongside the other docTypes, while the actual rendered-and-persisted document ac1 requires is produced by a1's separate Markdown composer -- the HTML registration becomes a secondary, effectively unused surface.
pros: Gives a nominal answer to 'is review-report a docgen docType' in both senses of the word
cons: Two renderers for one Story's one documented output is exactly the flexibility-nobody-asked-for this Story's own acceptance criteria (ac1-ac3) do not call for -- ac1 names one persisted MD artifact, not an HTML shell plus a separate MD file

The registered docType's RenderedDocumentShell output would be dead weight: nothing in ac1-ac3 ever reads or presents it, so it is pure unused surface area with its own maintenance cost (schema, registration, empty-diagram fields) for zero acceptance-criteria value
Violates 'no option, abstraction or flexibility nobody asked for' directly
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Technically satisfies every constraint by including a1's mechanism, but only by also building a second, acceptance-criteria-unused rendering path (a2's registry entry) purely for its own sake -- a direct instance of the flexibility-nobody-asked-for this Story's acceptance criteria do not call for, at the highest cost (L) for zero additional satisfied constraint.
